title: Suspected opioid overdose
summary: Call emergency services, give naloxone, and provide breaths and CPR without delay.
sources: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care — Opioid-Associated Emergency
actions: Check responsiveness and breathing. Call emergency services immediately and put the phone on speaker.
If breathing is absent or abnormal, start high-quality CPR with breaths. Use an AED as soon as available.
Give naloxone by the available approved route according to the device instructions. Naloxone must not delay CPR or emergency activation.
If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes and another dose is available, repeat according to the product instructions while continuing resuscitation.
If normal breathing returns but the person remains unresponsive, use the recovery position and monitor continuously. Stay until emergency responders arrive because overdose can recur.
prohibitions: Do not leave the person alone.
Do not use a cold shower, slapping, forced walking, or substances to “wake” the person.
Do not assume naloxone replaces medical assessment or CPR.

emergencyCall.text: Unresponsiveness with absent or abnormal breathing is a resuscitation emergency.
